title: Heaux Church by Brandon Kyle Goodman at Ars Nova #heauxchurch #arsnov...
transcript: Heaux Church at Ars Nova is not so much a service, but a celebration. Brandon Kyle Goodman, with the assistance of DJ Ari Grooves and some anatomical puppets, leads us through a journey that focuses on self-love and liberation from our shame. For Brandon, a big part of achieving this liberation is learning how to be a “heaux” — specifically with the bougie spelling. In this context, it has nothing to do with one's promiscuity or lack thereof, but rather one's commitment to thoughtfully interrogating their relationship to sex. The show is full of laughter, some audience participation, and some anecdotes from Brandon's life that give a loosely narrative structure to the piece. And this is something that I wish was featured more, as it brings a level of specificity that I think the piece really needs in order to not fall flat. Many of the ideas presented here, I think are being preached to the choir, but Brandon's personal stories are what dramatically elevate the piece and give us something new to chew on. Regardless, the show is a good time and Brandon's magnetic authenticity and humor is what keeps you leaned in from start to finish. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Reviewer recommends with clear caveats — feels some ideas preach to the choir and wants more personal narrative, but praises Brandon's magnetism and calls it a good time.
